debt-to-capital ratio (D/C ratio) is the ratio of its total debt to its total capital, its debt and [equity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equity_(finance)) combined.

debt-to-income ratio (DTI) is the percentage of a consumer's monthly [gross income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_income) that goes toward paying [debt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debt)s.
debtors days [ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratio) measures how quickly [cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cash) is being collected from [debtor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debtor)s.
